title: DARE before parameter-superposition unbinding
hypothesis: DARE sparsification followed by context binding into one shared delta tensor can retain per-task held-out function quality at lower complete serialized state than independent DARE deltas; structured Mirror contexts must beat standard Parameter Superposition contexts at matched bytes to establish incremental value.
physical_object: one shared base parameter vector and one superposed task-delta vector
mirror_coordinate: per-task deterministic sign context generated from task ID and context seed; unbinding is elementwise context multiplication
controls: Parameter Superposition without DARE using random Rademacher contexts
DARE then Parameter Superposition using random Rademacher contexts
native Parameter Superposition with identical contexts and unbinding

development.selection_metric: held-out per-task output NRMSE, complete serialized payload bytes, DARE-relative error, context interference and decode operations

paid_objects: independent sparse DARE indices and values

success_gate: At task count >=8 and at least one private fraction across all audit seeds, DARE+PS payload <=75% independent DARE payload, mean output NRMSE <= independent DARE NRMSE +.02, and unbind compute <=1.25x DARE decode. Mirror-specific value additionally requires strict advantage over byte-near standard PS/native context control; exact alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific attribution.
failure_gate: DARE+PS fails quality/storage/compute gates or is matched by standard/native Parameter Superposition; report task-count/interference frontier and do not infer independent capacity from number of addresses.
boundaries: Synthetic linear task deltas; no pretrained model fine-tuning, language benchmark, or actual task-merge claim.
Contexts are deterministic from code version, master seed and task ID; paid seed, IDs and metadata are serialized.
Shared base is included in every complete payload; no common-base state is treated as free.
No GPU or production runtime conclusion; operation counts are analytic proxies.
